BiblicalUsage: A stroke is a battering ram, and Ezekiel uses the word once, of the engines of war set against the walls of Tyre: he shall set engines of war against thy walls, and with his axes he shall break down thy towers.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the battering ram is the end of a city that trusted its walls: Tyre was strong on the sea, and God brought the ram to its gates, and no wall stands when He sends the breaker.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
